title: Fate Marable's calliope on the excursion boats
summary: He heard Fate Marable's calliope concerts before departure around 1921, and describes how the steam calliope was played.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Back to New Orleans. Yes. Did you hear any bands on excursion boats down on the river when you were a kid? Did you hear anything? No, it was great.

I heard Faith Marable. I used to give this concert at every even around 7 o'clock before the boat was depart. 7 or 8 o'clock. Half hour concert. You could hear it all over the city. Distinctly. As far as probably at the lakefront you could hear this callio. And he played all the current popular tunes. And he'd swing out. I think he was probably one of the greatest callio players of all, all time.
Now how old were you when that happened?
I was about 10 or 11 years old. It was about 19, 1921. I was about to say, I don't know.
Any other people play county out that you know?

Well all the guys that work on the river boats. Similar to a county, it's not a very hard deal. But it's, it's, uh, Wicked by steam. Steam boiler. And there's copper keys on it. You have to play it with gloves on. And a raincoat and a rain hat. Over your uniform. Your band uniform. Because the steam came from all directions. And the keys get awfully, awfully hot. That's why you use copper keys. And this copper, you have to be careful. This copper would get in your skin. One piano player, I think it was Fats Pichio. First time to put that raincoat on and play the callio up, you didn't realize that the keys was hot. It's cost his finger sound. He kept holding some whole notes over there. Some long notes. Yeah. The callio position you have to hit the staccato, you know. Faith can maneuver it because you played it so long.
It was a real haunting sound there in the evening.
